QF.id: SIA Case Studies on SAS Standards_32

question.text: An SE partners with a state government scheme on women's empowerment. Under SAS-400, the "deadweight" that the SIA should consider when assessing the SE's contribution is:

answer.text: The proportion of the reported outcome that would have happened anyway, irrespective of the SE's intervention, due to the government scheme or other factors
The number of SIAs on the panel

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook directs the assessor to evaluate whether evidenced changes are traceable to the intervention, how much could have happened irrespective of the intervention, what would have happened in the absence of the project, and to use deadweight to avoid overclaiming. Option A captures this directly. The Trap: Programme cost (Option B), evaluation cost (Option C), and the size of the SIA panel (Option D) are not deadweight; they are unrelated cost or governance items. Note: Anchor the deadweight discussion to the workbook's traceability, absence-of-project, contribution and overclaiming language rather than to specific named methods, and document the basis for the estimate transparently.
